title: Pulse-width modulation did not establish improved respiratory-rate fusion across BIDMC and CapnoBase
abstract: Adding half-prominence pulse-width modulation to fixed three-modulation PPG fusion did not establish lower respiratory-rate error: BIDMC gain 0.028 breaths/min (95% CI -0.321 to 0.365); independent CapnoBase gain -0.056 (-0.602 to 0.493). A fixed, label-free estimator was evaluated on 53 intensive-care and 42 independent perioperative recordings using equal-record mean absolute error and paired record bootstrap intervals. Longer windows, a wider frequency band and a second BIDMC annotator did not establish benefit. This negative result concerns this width definition and fusion rule, not all respiratory information in pulse morphology.
